Synopsis:
Minsc's default dialogue. In the current entries, he reflects on his opinion of us and our adventures so far, as well as revealing a little of history.

Cluster Contexts:
- Minsc_InParty.json: The party has just finished a confrontation with the Guild, and Minsc—accompanied by his constant companion Boo—is reacting afterward. He reveals that the Stone Lord and he are somehow the same person and admits a mind‑worm has been twisting his thoughts, leaving him guilty and confused even as the player points out the cult’s manipulation. Minsc is wrestling with the idea that anyone (including himself) can contain both good and evil, but he defaults to his simple, action‑first morality and wants to "crack villainous skulls" rather than overthink it. Other companions (Lae'zel’s distrust, Astarion’s teasing, Gale or Halsin’s input) may be present off‑screen and could colour the tone of this conversation.
- Minsc_InParty_Nested_PersonalQuestions.json: Minsc's default dialogue. In the current entries, he reflects on his opinion of us and our adventures so far, as well as revealing a little of history.
- LOW_Guildhall_BossFriol_OM_Minsc_COM_OOM.json: Origin moment for Minsc + Jaheira with Boss Friol.After Minsc learns of the Zhentarim plans to overthrow Nine-Fingers, he returns to the Guildhall to confront their leader, Roah. She taunts him with his past evil deeds as the 'Stone Lord' - the player decideds whether to back Minsc and fight Roah, or let Roah's plan come to fruition for the 'greater good'.
- LOW_CountingHouse_Heist.json: The player finds Rakath Glitterbeard, head banker, and his cronies gathered around a chest congratulating one another on a trap well-sprung. The chest is a mimic, which they've used to capture and kill the crime boss The Stone Lord - or so they believe.The mimic bursts apart from the inside to reveal that the Stone Lord is none other than Minsc - and he's in the thrall of the Absolute. A doppelganger cultist is imitating his old friend Jaheira in an attempt to control him.
- Minsc_SWD.json: Minsc's speak with dead dialogue. If you mention Boo, you will never get him off the topic - just nodes of him lamenting Boo in various states of vague dead grief and rage.

context: The party has just finished a clash with the Guild, and Minsc—Boo at his side—is reeling from revelations about his past. He confesses that the Stone Lord and Minsc are the same person, and that a mind‑worm (the cult’s influence) has been twisting his thoughts; this leaves him guilty and confused even as the player insists the cult manipulated him. Minsc now wonders whether good and evil can coexist in anyone, but he defaults to a simple, action‑first morality and keeps insisting on “cracking villainous skulls” rather than overthinking things. Off‑screen events that feed into this moment include earlier confrontations where he was accused or revealed as the Stone Lord (and cultists even used a doppelganger of Jaheira in attempts to control him), and other companions’ reactions may colour the tone of the conversation.
